facts.rationale: Distinguishes the aerial target-item callback from the separately registered fighter-victim grab callback and matches the supported grounded item-callback naming.

evidence.why: Separate registrations, item setup, destinations, and opposite branch flags.
Resulting aerial phases use distinct item and victim getters.

facts.value: Advances the aerial item-target branch of Egg Lay into SpecialAirN2_1 when command variable 0 is set and the target item still exists. This is distinct from the fighter-victim branch, which advances to SpecialAirN2_0 and later enters the victim into the common YoshiEgg state.
facts.rationale: Corrects the baseline conflation of item-outcome article creation with opponent enclosure.

facts.value: Implements grounded completion of Egg Lay's item-target outcome: script commands can tear down the target-item association and create an It_Kind_Yoshi_EggLay article. Fighter-victim enclosure is handled separately by SpecialN2_0.
facts.rationale: Makes the demonstrated item-versus-victim distinction explicit without changing supported command-processing knowledge.

evidence.why: Grounded article creation and separate victim handoff.

facts.rationale: Names the returned HSD_Joint model definition rather than implying a live HSD_JObj.

evidence.why: Definition is consumed to construct and attach the victim's accessory.

facts.value: Supplies the Egg Lay victim's scale-interpolation coefficient. The initializer stores x1C in mv.co.yoshiegg.xC; the accessory callback uses it in the shared multiplier (1 - xC) + ((x10 - x14) / x10) * xC applied separately to the saved fighter-model and egg-accessory scales.
facts.rationale: Replaces the stale unidentified-only mapping with the directly demonstrated consumer role, without claiming a configured numeric value.

evidence.why: Exact interpolation formula and separate scale consumers.

facts.value: Supplies Egg Lay duration tuning: item-outcome construction copies this per-fighter x24 value into the article's lifetime, and common YoshiEgg victim initialization passes it to ftCommon_InitGrab. The corresponding canonical Kirby copied-move accessor names its value specialn_ys_base_duration; this does not establish an exact configured duration or the complete grab-duration formula.
facts.rationale: Adds useful demonstrated lifetime/base-duration semantics while preserving uncertainty about units and downstream computation.

facts.value: Returns the per-fighter Egg Lay growth interval stored as the victim's mv.co.yoshiegg.x10. The accessory callback uses it as the denominator of a scale-progress expression, applying the resulting multiplier separately to the saved fighter-model and egg-accessory scales. It does not interpolate one object's scale into the other's.
facts.rationale: Corrects the baseline's model-to-egg-scale explanation while retaining the supported growth-interval role. The unusual x14 initialization remains unnormalized.

evidence.why: Separate scale vectors and interval denominator.
x10 assignment and unusual x14 initialization.

facts.rationale: The typedef-int bool accessor forwards a duration value rather than a normalized flag; the release consumer uses it as an integer countdown-extension input.

facts.value: Parameterless accessor declared bool(void). In this project's C headers bool is typedef int, so the effective return domain is integer and the direct x38 return is not normalized to zero or one. The release caller passes it to an int duration parameter.
facts.rationale: Corrects a factual type-domain error without changing the canonical declaration.

facts.value: Returns Yoshi's global extended-attribute x38 unchanged through the project's integer bool type. At victim timer expiry, ftCo_YoshiEgg_Anim passes the result to ftColl_8007B760, which replaces x1990 only if the supplied integer is larger, then sets x198C to numeric state 2 and invokes ftCo_800BFFD0 with 9 and 0. No zero-or-one conversion occurs in this path.
facts.rationale: Preserves the supported source, release consumer, and max-only update while removing the false boolean-normalization claim and keeping numeric states explicit.

evidence.why: Exact integer update and numeric state.

facts.value: Provides Yoshi's configured integer duration input for the victim's temporary collision-status setup at Egg Lay breakout. Despite the bool spelling, it returns x38 without restricting the value to zero or one.
facts.rationale: Corrects the prior zero-versus-one interpretation and states the demonstrated role without asserting a configured value.

facts.value: When the victim's grab_timer is nonpositive, the YoshiEgg animation callback performs breakout effects and velocity/model restoration, passes this getter's unchanged integer result to ftColl_8007B760, and then enters the YoshiEgg fall path. The collision helper selects numeric state 2 and only extends x1990 when the supplied duration exceeds its current value; the getter itself is stateless.
facts.rationale: Retains release ordering and the exceptional max-only duration rule while removing the unsupported zero-or-one restriction.

evidence.why: Exact expiry guard and operation order.
Max-only duration update and state selection.

facts.value: Supplies Egg Lay's victim-release protection-duration setting to the common breakout path. It is an integer-valued configuration input, not a zero-or-one flag; the visible consumer selects collision-status state 2 and extends its associated countdown only when the requested value is larger.
facts.rationale: Corrects the baseline's restricted-domain claim while preserving the release-protection interpretation and explicit numeric consumer behavior.

evidence.why: Numeric protection-state setup and countdown extension.
